title: 7 Signs Mom or Dad Needs Help at Home (and What to Do Next)
short_title: 7 signs Mom or Dad needs help at home
description: Something feels a little off when you visit Mom or Dad? Here are 7 signs a parent may need help at home, plus how to start the conversation and how to start small.
end: A free in-home assessment is the first step.

parts.head: 7 signs Mom or Dad needs help at home
parts.text: You visit Mom or Dad, and something feels a little off. Maybe it's small. Maybe it's been building for a while. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. Here are seven signs that a parent may need some help at home, and what to do next.

parts.head: The kitchen
parts.sub: Expired food, very little food, the same meal every day
parts.text: Number one: the kitchen. Open the fridge. Expired food, very little food, or the same meal over and over can mean cooking has gotten hard. Weight loss is a sign, too.

parts.head: The mail
parts.sub: Unopened stacks, late notices, bills paid twice
parts.text: Number two: the mail. Stacks of unopened mail, late notices, or bills paid twice can mean the paperwork is getting confusing.

parts.head: The house
parts.sub: Dishes, laundry and clutter piling up
parts.text: Number three: the house. If someone who always kept a tidy home now has dishes piling up, laundry everywhere, or a strong smell, the chores may have become too much.

parts.head: Getting ready for the day
parts.sub: Same clothes, bathing less, skipping old routines
parts.text: Number four: getting ready for the day. Wearing the same clothes for days, bathing less, or skipping the things they always did, like doing their hair, often means bathing and dressing have become hard, or even scary.

parts.head: Falls and close calls
parts.sub: Bruises, holding onto furniture, a fall they didn't mention
parts.text: Number five: falls and close calls. Bruises they can't explain, holding onto the furniture to get across the room, or a fall they didn't tell you about. Falls are one of the biggest reasons seniors lose their independence, so take them seriously.

parts.head: Medicine
parts.sub: Bottles still full, or empty too soon
parts.text: Number six: medicine. Pill bottles that are still full, or empty too soon, or a pill organizer with days missed. Medicine mistakes can be dangerous.

parts.head: Pulling away
parts.sub: Skipping church, cards, calls with friends
parts.text: Number seven: pulling away. Skipping church, dropping out of card club, or not calling friends anymore. Sometimes it's because getting out has gotten hard, and being alone that much is hard on anyone.

parts.head: You
parts.sub: Driving over every day, losing sleep, always worried
parts.text: And one more sign people forget: you. If you're the one driving over every day, losing sleep, and worrying all the time, that matters, too.

parts.head: Sudden change? Call the doctor first.
parts.sub: An infection or a medicine can cause it
parts.text: A quick note. If any of these changes happen suddenly, call their doctor first. A sudden change in memory or behavior can be caused by an infection or a medicine.

parts.head: Start with a gentle conversation
parts.text: So what do you do next? Start with a gentle conversation, not a verdict. Instead of saying, you can't live alone anymore, try asking, what would make your days easier? Most parents want to stay home, and a little help at home can be how they do.

parts.head: Start small
parts.sub: A few hours a week: meals, housekeeping, rides, bathing
parts.text: You don't have to start with all-day care. Many families start with a few hours a week: help with meals and light housekeeping, a ride to the store, or help with bathing. You can add more as needs change.

parts.head: A free in-home assessment
parts.sub: Then meet your caregiver's profile before the first visit
parts.text: At Caring Companions, it starts with a free in-home assessment. We get to know your parent and your family, and build a care plan around what matters most. Before the first visit, we send you your caregiver's profile with a friendly photo, so Mom never opens the door to a stranger.
We serve families in Springfield and across southwest Missouri. Call us at (417) 234-8494, or visit mo-care.com. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
